title: Why Does a Pen Cap Have a Tiny Hole?
parts: Pick up that pen again. Look at the cap. See the tiny hole?
You have probably seen it a thousand times, and never thought about it.
It is not there for the ink. According to its maker, it is there for safety.
It is a very small hole with a very serious job.
So why does a pen cap have a tiny hole?
Children put things in their mouths, and a pen cap is small enough to fit.
If a cap is inhaled by accident, it can block the airway.
A twenty twenty-four case series in a medical journal describes three children, aged four, thirteen and fourteen, who inhaled pen caps. Removing them took demanding procedures.
The authors point out that the cone shape of a pen cap can make it lodge in the airway.
That report does not say whether those caps had a hole. We cite it only to show the danger is real.
Here is where the hole comes in. Wikipedia reports that since nineteen ninety-one, the classic Bic Cristal pen has had a small hole in its cap.
The reason, in the company's words as quoted by ScienceAlert, is to keep a cap from completely blocking the airway if it is accidentally inhaled.
Here is our reading. The hole is a tiny air path, so if a cap lodges in the throat, a little air may still get through.
That is not a guarantee. The company's words are about reducing the risk of a total blockage, not removing the danger.
And that date belongs to one pen. We do not claim every pen changed in nineteen ninety-one.
There is also an international standard about pen caps and asphyxiation, I S O eleven five forty.
The latest edition we found dates from August twenty twenty-one. Its title: Specification for caps to reduce the risk of asphyxiation.
It applies to writing and marking instruments that children of about fourteen and younger are likely to use. It does not cover pens meant only for adults.
We could not open the full text, so we will not describe its tests. We read only the title and the scope.
There is another hole, and it does something else.
On at least one Bic model, a tiny hole in the barrel keeps the air pressure the same inside and outside the pen, according to Wikipedia, citing the company's own FAQ.
So the barrel hole is about pressure, and the cap hole is mainly about breathing.
ScienceAlert adds that the cap hole also helps with air pressure when you close it. But the company's quote is about the airway.
A tiny hole with a quiet job is easy to miss.
Small holes are easy to ignore. That is exactly why they are worth noticing.
Next time you pick up a pen, check the cap. You may find the hole on some pens and not on others.
And if a small child is around, keep caps out of reach. The hole is meant to help, but it is not a promise.
So that tiny hole is not decoration. According to the company, it is a safety feature, quietly doing its job.
Even a safety detail can hide in plain sight. Think of the heavy door at the back of a cinema.
Why does it open outward, when you push a bar?
